title: Observability inventory + alert matrix — runtime edge cases (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a practical inventory of observability signals for the token-serving runtime and the supporting control plane, plus an alert matrix targeted at reducing noise while ensuring actionable coverage for production degradations. Focus areas: 1) runtime hot paths (inference request -> token emission), 2) routing & fallbacks (model variant routing), 3) cache behavior (prefix/KV cache), 4) infra/queueing/backpressure, and 5) control-plane anomalies (model-load failures, version rollouts).

Approach and constraints:
- Keep signal definitions strongly typed: metric name, unit, aggregation window, primary tag dimensions, example PromQL/SQL, owner, suggested alert thresholds.
- Aim for one authoritative alert per failure mode (severity + runbook), avoid duplicate alerts that rely on same metric.
- Prioritize alerts that reduce user-visible impact (errors, latencies) and that map directly to mitigations (kill/scale/route).
- Use noisy-tolerance strategies: dynamic thresholds (percentile over baseline), alert for rate-of-change rather than absolute value where appropriate, and multi-signal confirmation for low-SNR cases.

Inventory (selected signals) — runtime hot path:
1) inference.request.latency_p95_ms
   - unit: ms
   - aggregation: 5m p95 across hosts for route+model
   - dimensions: route, model_name, region, customer_tier
   - example query: p95_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~".*infer.*"}[5m])) by (le, route, model_name)), 5m)
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - why: direct user-facing latency SLO; sensitive to CPU/GPU contention and batching behavior

2) inference.request.error_rate
   - unit: errors per minute / percentage
   - aggregation: sum(errors)/sum(requests) over 5m per route
   - dimensions: route, model_name, error_class (500/timeout/kvcache_miss?)
   - example query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2..",route=~".*infer.*"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route=~".*infer.*"}[5m]))
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - why: triages model runtime failures vs infra; high priority for production routes

3) kvcache.local.hit_rate
   - unit: ratio
   - aggregation: rolling 15m average
   - dimensions: model_name, shard, region
   - example: 1 - (sum(kvcache_miss_count[15m]) / sum(kvcache_lookup_count[15m]))
   - owner: applied-ml
   - why: sudden drop often explains latency spikes and token growth cost; useful for fallback and cache-rewarm strategies

4) batching.effective_tokens_per_batch
   - unit: tokens per batch (float)
   - aggregation: mean over 5m
   - dimensions: model_name, instance_type
   - why: under-batching increases cost; sudden drop may indicate routing to smaller pools or request skew

5) gpu.utilization_pct_per_instance
   - unit: percent
   - aggregation: 1m avg, alert on sustained >95% for 3m or sustained <10% for unexpected nodes
   - dimensions: instance_id, pool
   - why: high util => contention; low util on busy pool => placement failure or metric drift

Control plane / rollouts:
6) model.deploy.load_failures_total
   - unit: count (per deploy)
   - why: catch model artifact issues early; tie to rollout window and auto-rollbacks

7) routing.fallback_rate
   - unit: percentage of requests routed to fallback variants
   - why: when fallback spikes, investigate upstream model variant compatibility or capacity constraints

Alert matrix (example mappings) — severity tiers and triggers:
- Sev P0 (page): SLI breach with customer impact + automatic mitigation absent
  * inference.request.error_rate > 3% for top-10 routes for 5m AND p95 latency > 2x baseline --> page oncall (eng-sre)
  * model.deploy.load_failures_total > 5 within 15m for a rollout tagged prod --> page product-ops + applied-ml
- Sev P1 (on-call notify + Slack): high probability of user impact, automated fallback available
  * inference.request.latency_p95_ms > SLO * 1.5 for a route for 10m -> alert to eng-serving-runtime; automatic fallback to smaller model variant if configured
  * kvcache.local.hit_rate drops >20% vs 1h rolling baseline AND request.error_rate increases 0.5% -> alert to applied-ml
- Sev P2 (ticket): resource or soft degradation; investigate next business day
  * gpu.utilization_pct_per_instance < 10% for >30m across >30% of pool -> create ticket (possible placement/healthcheck issue)
  * batching.effective_tokens_per_batch drops by 40% on a high-volume route -> ticket to platform-engineering to review routing policy

Noise reduction heuristics built into alerts:
- Require corroboration: for low-precision metrics (e.g., kvcache hit-rate) pair with a second signal (latency or error increase) before paging.
- Adaptive thresholds: alert on relative change vs a 1h or 24h baseline rather than absolute thresholds for spikes that correlate with traffic growth.
- Grouping by owner: set alert grouping keys to route+model_name to avoid N alerts when one root cause affects many instances.
- Suppression windows: suppress rollout-related alerts for a configured window when an active rollout job is running (but still log and label them so postmortem can see them).

Tracing and spans (notes for instrumenting traces to reduce investigation time):
- Key trace root: request_id -> route -> model_name -> serving_instance -> kernel_exec -> kvcache_lookup -> token_emit.
- Required spans and attributes:
  * span/http.receive: attributes {route, model_name, customer_id, input_tokens}
  * span/queue.wait: {queue_depth, deadline_ms}
  * span/kvcache.lookup: {hit=true/false, key_prefix_len, shard}
  * span/kernel.exec: {seq_len, beam_size, gpu_mem_mb, quantized=true/false}
  * span/token.emit: {tokens_emitted, stream=true/false}
- Trace sampling policy: 1% global sampling for perf, 100% for errors and any request with latency > p99_slo*1.5, 100% for rollout-deployed requests (with rollout tag).
- Enrich traces with rollout tags and config revision so post-deploy regressions are easy to correlate.

Dashboard composition checklist (single-pane-of-glass per route):
- Top row: traffic volume (rps), request p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, SLO burn rate
- Middle row: kvcache hit-rate, batching tokens-per-batch, GPU util %, queue depth
- Bottom row: recent traces (sample links), deployment status, recent alerts and active incidents
- Panel rules: every threshold on the dashboard should be linked to an alert definition (one-to-one mapping).

Runbooks and first-responder playbook (short):
- If p0 page for high error rate: 1) check top-5 routes and recent deploys (concurrent deploys often cause artifact mismatch), 2) check model.load_failures and instance logs, 3) failover route to fallback variant or increase capacity in Dedicated pools, 4) if rollback needed, follow deploy rollback playbook.
- If kvcache hit-rate falls: 1) search traces for kvcache.lookup misses with the same key prefix; 2) inspect recent model changes that could change tokenization/prefix patterns; 3) consider cache rewarm (warm requests synthetic) or reduce TTLs on cache invalidation windows.

Open questions / next steps (action items):
- Decide canonical metric names and Prometheus histogram bucket conventions for token latency vs total request latency. (owner: eng-observability)
- Implement multi-signal alert templates in PagerDuty with suppression and re-notify rules. (owner: eng-sre)
- Add rollout tagging to all traces and HTTP metrics (owner: platform-engineering)
- Prototype dynamic baseline alert (percentile vs rolling window) for kvcache hit-rate and batching metrics. (owner: applied-ml + eng-serving-runtime)

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Could we derive a single composite SLI for token-serving health that weights latency, error rate, and token cost? Would help exec-level dashboards.
- Investigate anomaly-detection-based alerting for low-traffic routes to reduce manual threshold tuning.

References and useful links:
- telemetry repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/78
- rollout policies doc (confluence): CON-obs-inventory-3
- related tickets: JIRA-OBS-452

End of draft.

(Reasonably informal — meant to be iterated in the observability working group; please leave inline comments rather than editing raw thresholds until we standardize naming.)
